Leonardo, this is Diane Okafor at Halversen Group. Thursday is confirmed, and I want to be useful, so let me tell you who is in that room and what they will do to you. Six people. Two of them have read your note, and four of them have read the first page of it. The chair will give you twelve minutes and she will not give you thirteen. Now, three things. First, open with the recommendation, not with the background. If you walk us through the history, you will lose the room before you reach the scenarios. Second, when you present the three scenarios, distinguish clearly between what the law requires and what the authority is likely to do in practice. Our finance director will not follow you if you blend the two, and he is the one who signs. Third, and I mean this kindly. You will be interrupted. It is not hostility, it is how this board works. Anticipate the two questions everybody always asks, which are what it costs and when we have to decide, and answer them before they are asked. And when you close, sum up in one sentence. One. If you need two sentences, the position is not clear yet. Send me the deck on Wednesday morning and I will tell you where the board will push.

I examine speaking tests, and I want to describe the candidate I meet at the end of a course like yours, because you probably cannot see him yourself. Fourteen weeks ago you were translating. Now you are not, and I can usually hear where that changed, somewhere around the tenth session, when people hit their stride and stop asking whether the sentence is correct while they are still saying it. Here is what I actually listen for on the day. Not vocabulary. Three things. First, whether you can hold a long turn. Two minutes on one idea, with a beginning and an end, and no sentence abandoned halfway. Second, whether you repair yourself. Every candidate makes mistakes. The strong ones say let me rephrase that and keep going in three words. The weak ones stop and apologize, and that costs more marks than the error ever did. And third, connected speech. Not an accent. Nobody is asking you to sound American. But if you say every word separately, in blocks, with a pause between each one, the listener has to work, and a tired examiner at four in the afternoon hears effort instead of content. So link the words you already have. One last thing. On the day you will not learn anything new. Everything you use will be something you already own. What decides the score is whether you can pull it all together for fourteen minutes without stopping.

Thank you for the time. Let me sum up our recommendation in one sentence before I show you anything. I will synthesize the three scenarios we modelled and give you the numbers behind each one. Before I transition to the second half, let me distinguish between what the law requires and what the authority does in practice. The team advised the finance director in March to avoid signing any new intercompany agreement, and that advice stands. To pull it all together, the decision is manageable, and it is only manageable if it is taken this quarter.
